name: Environment & Ecology
description: Ecology, conventions, protected areas and environmental issues.

questions.question: Which was India's first Ramsar site, designated in 1981?
questions.explanation: Chilika (Odisha) and Keoladeo (Rajasthan) were India's first two Ramsar sites in 1981; India now has 80+ wetlands of international importance.

questions.question: Which is India's largest Ramsar site?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans mangrove wetland is India's largest Ramsar site; it spans West Bengal and supports the Royal Bengal Tiger.

questions.question: Project Elephant, for the protection of wild elephants and their corridors, was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: Project Elephant began in 1992 (a centrally sponsored scheme), complementing Project Tiger (1973).

questions.question: CITES is an international agreement regulating trade in what?
options: Endangered species of flora and fauna
questions.explanation: CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species, 1973) lists species in Appendices I–III to control their trade.

questions.question: The UNFCCC, the parent treaty of the Paris Agreement, was adopted at which summit?
questions.explanation: The UN Framework Convention on Climate Change was adopted at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit and entered into force in 1994.

questions.question: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) is famous for imposing what on developed countries?
questions.explanation: Kyoto set binding emission targets for industrialised ('Annex I') countries under the principle of 'common but differentiated responsibilities'.

questions.question: The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to keep global temperature rise this century well below what, and pursue efforts to limit it further?
questions.explanation: Article 2 of the Paris Agreement: hold warming well below 2°C and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C, through NDCs.

questions.question: COP30 (2025), the first UN climate conference held in the Amazon region, took place in which Brazilian city?
questions.explanation: COP30 was held in Belém, Pará (November 2025) — symbolically, at the gateway to the Amazon rainforest.

questions.question: At COP26, India committed to achieving net-zero emissions by which year?
questions.explanation: PM Modi's 'Panchamrit' at Glasgow (2021) included net-zero by 2070, 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, and 50% renewables.

questions.question: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established in which year?
questions.explanation: The NGT (National Green Tribunal Act, 2010) is a specialised body for expeditious disposal of environmental cases.

questions.question: The lion-tailed macaque, an endangered primate, is endemic to which region?
questions.explanation: The lion-tailed macaque (Macaca silenus) lives only in the rainforests of the Western Ghats — a biodiversity hotspot.

questions.question: The Great Indian Bustard, a critically endangered bird, is mainly found in the grasslands of which state?
questions.explanation: The GIB's last strongholds are the Desert National Park area (Rajasthan); power lines remain its biggest threat.

questions.question: Silent Valley National Park, famous for its pristine rainforests, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Silent Valley (Kerala) was saved from a hydroelectric project after the 'Save Silent Valley' movement of the 1970s–80s.

questions.question: Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO site, is world-famous for which animal?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga (Assam) hosts about two-thirds of the world's Indian one-horned rhinos, plus tigers, elephants and swamp deer.

questions.question: Which chemical gas leaked in the 1984 Bhopal disaster, one of the world's worst industrial accidents?
questions.explanation: Methyl isocyanate leaked from the Union Carbide plant on 2–3 December 1984, killing thousands and leading to the Bhopal Gas Tragedy Act.
